description: NOT before an IS-led simple relational operator with no NOT of its own in an abbreviated combined relation condition (A > B AND NOT IS > C OR D). At 85 the NOT is the logical operator (§1985:VI.6.3.3 GRL2.2: the word after it is IS, not GREATER, >, LESS, <, EQUAL or =), so the tail is (NOT (A > C)) and > is carried. ISO 2002 prints [NOT] simple-relational-operator in the abbreviated tail (§2002:8.8.4.2.4.1) and GR2 b) of §2002:8.8.4.2.4.3 makes the NOT part of the simple relational operator, so at 2002 the tail is (A NOT > C) and NOT > is carried. The 2014 general format (§2014:8.8.4.2.4.1) drops the bracketed NOT, so from 2014 the shape is in no format: COBOL0902 (a warning under --permissive, the 2002 meaning kept). The other shapes of the grammar's negatedAbbreviatedRelation node are abbreviated-not-logical-removed-2002; NegatedAbbreviationForms.Of partitions the two (kb/Work PB5123, review R1-1).
display: NOT before an IS-led simple relational operator in an abbreviated relation
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMANOTIS.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 A PIC 9 VALUE 5.
01 B PIC 9 VALUE 1.
01 C PIC 9 VALUE 6.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    IF A > B AND NOT IS > C
        DISPLAY "TRUE"
    END-IF.
    STOP RUN.
